newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees no public sector pay rise for now.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees no public sector pay rise for now.

text.p: Brazil's federal government considers it impossible to contemplate a public sector pay rise for the moment, a Planning Ministry spokeswoman said.

"In the current circumstances, without approval of the civil service reforms or the Fiscal Stabilization Fund (FEF), it is difficult to think about a general wage hike for the public sector," the spokeswoman said.
She said news reports quoting the head of the ministry's economics department Amaury Bier as completely ruling out any salary adjustments this year were not totally accurate.
"Amaury says he might have said there was no possibility of a general wage rise given the circumstances," she said.
The government has expressed its desire to eliminate some salary distortions that occur within the civil service.
Police chiefs in the Federal District, for example, earn $20,000 a month while many management-level officials earn $3,650 a month, far less than their private sector equivalents.
Federal government payroll costs in 1997 have been fixed at 45.1 billion reais, up from 41.5 billion reais in 1996, and officials say that amount will not be exceeded.
